questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is an example of the factor of production capital?

options.A: a bank account held by a small firm to be used for future purchases
options.B: a forest of hardwood trees ideal for furniture making
options.C: the market value of a company’s shares
options.D: word processing software used by a writer to complete her new book

questions.questionText: What is the opportunity cost to an unemployed worker who becomes employed?

options.A: the leisure they would otherwise have had
options.B: the value of the goods and services they produce
options.C: the wages they are paid
options.D: zero

questions.questionText: Which statement is normative?

options.A: As a general rule, people are happier in more equal societies.
options.B: Despite a large increase in income per head, people are no happier today than they were 50 years ago.
options.C: Happiness depends not on the absolute level of a person’s income but on his relative income.
options.D: The promotion of happiness is a more important goal than the maximisation of production.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a demand curve for a good. price D O quantity Which statement describes the nature of this demand curve?

options.A: A fall in price is the result of a fall in demand.
options.B: A greater or smaller quantity is demanded as price changes.
options.C: As demand increases so does price.
options.D: Quantity changes in proportion to the change in price.

questions.questionText: How would an economist establish the market demand curve for a private good?

options.A: by adding consumer surplus to total expenditure
options.B: by combining individual demand curves horizontally
options.C: by combining the price elasticity of individual demands
options.D: by multiplying price by quantity demanded

questions.questionText: What could cause a shift in the supply curve of good X and a movement along its supply curve? shift in the curve movement along the curve

options.A: a change in consumer preferences an increase in the price of a substitute good
options.B: a decrease in factor productivity the imposition of a tax on good X
options.C: an increase in the price of a an increase in factor productivity complementary good
options.D: an increase in the wage rates a change in consumer preferences in the industry

questions.questionText: The price of good X rises by 10%. As a result, the demand for a complementary good Y changes by 20%. What is the cross elasticity of demand for good Y with respect to good X?
An industry is comprised of three firms, R, S and T which produce product X. price of X output of X $ firm R firm S firm T 36 80 59 85
52 0 68 By how much is a rise in the price of product X from $22 to $36 likely to increase the market supply of X?
A firm estimates that the price elasticity of supply of its product is 0.4. Should the firm be concerned by this figure?

options.A: No, as it implies that the firm will be able to raise revenue by raising price.
options.B: No, as it suggests there are few substitutes for the product.
options.C: Yes, as it indicates that the firm is not able to adjust supply easily when demand changes.
options.D: Yes, as it means that demand for its product is increasing at a slow rate.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows three supply curves. S price S S O quantity What can be concluded about the price elasticity of supply of the curves?

options.A: As price rises, the price elasticity of supply of S will increase.
options.B: At any price, the price elasticity of supply of S will be less than that of S .

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect on the market for rice of a change in government policy that causes a shift in the supply curve from S to S . S S L price K J M D O quantity What does the area JKLM represent?

options.A: the additional saving to importers of the removal of a tariff on rice
options.B: the cost to the government of a subsidy to rice growers
options.C: the increase in consumer surplus from the introduction of a maximum price for rice
options.D: the loss in government revenue from the reduction in a lump sum tax on rice

questions.questionText: What is necessary for consumer surplus to be zero?

options.A: Demand is perfectly elastic.
options.B: Demand is perfectly inelastic.
options.C: Supply is perfectly elastic.
options.D: Supply is perfectly inelastic.

questions.questionText: In a free market in equilibrium, the production of the good illustrated below imposes an external cost upon society. Which letter could represent the total cost of producing the free market equilibrium output? S (marginal B private cost) A price C D

options.D: (marginal private benefit) O output

questions.questionText: The table shows, for two different quantities of good X, the total amount consumers are willing to pay and the total external benefits that are generated. quantity of good X consumers’ willingness total external benefits (units) to pay ($) ($)
What is a merit good?

options.A: a good that is made available to consumers according to merit
options.B: a good that the government believes consumers will buy too little of if it is provided by private enterprise at market prices
options.C: a good where any benefit obtained by one consumer is extended to all consumers
options.D: a good where the private benefits of consuming the good exceed its social benefits

questions.questionText: Which good or service is excludable but non-rival in consumption?

options.A: fish stocks
options.B: national defence
options.C: street lighting
options.D: TV broadcasting

questions.questionText: What must a government do to stabilise the price of an agricultural commodity? when demand exceeds supply when supply exceeds demand

options.A: add the excess demand to a buffer stock release an amount equal to the excess supply from a buffer stock
options.B: meet excess demand by running purchase the excess supply and down a buffer stock add it to a buffer stock
options.C: subsidise production impose a tax on consumers
options.D: tax consumers of the commodity subsidise production

questions.questionText: The world consists of Sealand and Fantasia. Each produces two goods, X and Y. Good X needs much land but little labour. Good Y needs much labour but little land. Sealand has plentiful land and labour. Fantasia has more labour than Sealand. What can be deduced from the above about Sealand?

options.A: It is unlikely to gain from trade with Fantasia.
options.B: It will have an absolute advantage in the production of both X and Y.
options.C: It will have a comparative advantage in the production of X.
options.D: It will have a comparative advantage in the production of Y.

questions.questionText: Which measure would encourage domestic production?

options.A: the safety standards for imports.
options.B: the size of import quotas.
options.C: the subsidies on home produced goods.
options.D: the time taken to process import paperwork.

questions.questionText: Which combination of export and import prices will cause the greatest change in a country’s terms of trade? export prices import prices

options.A: decrease by 1% increase by 1%
options.B: decrease by 2% no change
options.C: increase by 1% decrease by 1%
options.D: no change increase by 2%

questions.questionText: Unemployment is usually divided into two categories: long-term (more than 12 months) and short-term (less than 12 months). The diagram shows the long-term unemployment rate as a percentage of total unemployment for four countries between 2002 and 2007. W W X Y long-term 40 unemployment (% of total) 30 Y X Z Z 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 What is correct about unemployment from the diagram?

options.A: Country W had the lowest percentage of short-term unemployment.
options.B: Country X was least successful in reducing the percentage of long-term unemployment.
options.C: Country Y was least successful in reducing the percentage of short-term unemployment.
options.D: Country Z had the highest percentage of long-term unemployment.

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual percentage change in an index of prices. country 2008 2009 China 6.3 –1.2 Pakistan 24.3 11.2 Saudi Arabia 10.9 10.7 United States 5.6 –1.4 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Prices were lowest in the United States in both 2008 and 2009.
options.B: Prices were most stable in Saudi Arabia.
options.C: The fall in inflation between 2008 and 2009 was greater in China than Saudi Arabia.
options.D: The price of all products sold by Chinese firms fell in 2009.

questions.questionText: Which combination is likely to result from demand-pull inflation? balance of trade profits

options.A: improving falling
options.B: improving rising
options.C: worsening falling
options.D: worsening rising

questions.questionText: In 2008-9 American households reduced their consumption of domestic and imported goods and used part of the money to pay back some of their debts. Which outcome could be consistent with this change?

options.A: a decline in the US trade deficit
options.B: a decrease in savings
options.C: a decrease in the US terms of trade
options.D: a decrease in unemployment

questions.questionText: A country’s floating exchange rate falls and its export revenue declines. What could explain this?

options.A: Demand for its exports is inelastic.
options.B: Supply of its exports is elastic.
options.C: The exchange rate is in disequilibrium.
options.D: The price of exports, in terms of foreign currency, rises.

questions.questionText: In the diagram the foreign exchange market is initially in equilibrium at X. What could be the new equilibrium position after an increase in demand from US residents for holidays in Europe? S S S price A B of US$ (in Euros) X C D

options.D: D
